summary: Describes the LDAP / X.500 entryDN operational attribute, which gives a copy of an entry's distinguished name for use in attribute value assertions. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5020 defines the LDAP entryDN operational attribute, which holds a copy of an entry's distinguished name. Searches can use that copy in filters, but clients cannot change the DN through the attribute.

subtitle: An LDAP operational attribute that stores a copy of an entry's distinguished name.

tldr.problem: An LDAP entry's distinguished name identifies it, but the DN is not itself an attribute that can be tested in an attribute assertion.
tldr.mechanism: The entryDN operational attribute provides a copy of the entry's current DN so it can be used in search filters.
tldr.outcome: The attribute is generated for directory operation, has one value, and cannot be modified through entryDN.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 5020's status as Proposed Standard. The RFC defines the LDAP entryDN operational attribute.

sections.title: Making an Entry's DN Searchable
sections.content:
In X.500 directory services, an entry is identified by its distinguished name (DN). But because the DN is not an attribute of the entry, an LDAP filter cannot make an ordinary attribute-value assertion against it.

The entryDN operational attribute provides a copy of the entry's current DN. The RFC gives an example using component matching to select entries under particular directory subtrees.
sections.plainLanguage: An entry has a name that identifies its place in the directory. This attribute copies that name so a search can test it.

sections.title: Properties of entryDN
sections.content:
The RFC defines entryDN as a single-valued operational attribute with distinguished-name matching. Its value is a copy of the entry's current DN, and the attribute is not available for user modification.

The DN cannot be changed through this attribute. The attribute provides another way to access the entry's name, rather than a separate name that can be edited.
sections.plainLanguage: The directory supplies one current DN value for the entry. Users cannot edit the DN by changing this attribute.

sections.title: Using entryDN in a Search
sections.content:
An LDAP client can include entryDN in a search filter to select entries based on where they appear in the directory. The RFC's example searches a subtree while matching entries whose distinguished names contain one of two specified components.

The attribute is intended for attribute-value assertions and does not change the DN model or how entries are identified in the directory.
sections.plainLanguage: A search can use entryDN to find entries by their directory names. The attribute adds a way to test the DN without making it editable.
